abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the 2-adic zeta value ζ₂(7) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The value is defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), so zeta2 7 = J(6)/768; the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. ζ₂(3) and ζ₂(5) are known to be irrational, and L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025) proved that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational; the theorem here implies that result and the two registered formalisations of the same maintainer for {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11)} and {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9)}. An unrefereed draft by C. D. Long claims, by a different method, that ζ₂(s) is irrational for every odd s with 3 ≤ s ≤ 29; it is not used here, and an internal review of it (docs/long_review.md) found a gap in its large-prime step, so we do not regard it as settling the question. No refereed proof that ζ₂(7) is irrational is known to us. The proof uses the linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2−n/2) dt = ρ_n + Z_n ζ₂(7) of the rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} Π_{c∈C_m} (t+1/2+c) / Π_{k=0}^{n} (t+k)^(a_k), with six nested well-poised numerator blocks C_m = [η_m n, (1−η_m) n − 1], η = (5, 7, 7, 9, 11, 13)/40, and pole orders a_k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} that ramp up from both ends; the evaluation at the centred point t + 1/2 − n/2 leaves ζ₂(7) as the only zeta value. The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus, and the size of the coefficients from residue-level Cauchy bounds and a certified maximum of an explicit potential. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by a residue-class analysis of the partial fractions (a class lemma, a kernel identity and per-pole bounds, evaluated on local models of the residue classes whose values are certified in Lean on finitely many intervals) and the prime number theorem, proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem. If ζ₂(7) were rational, the valuations at the auxiliary prime ℓ = 19n/20 − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

related_formalizations.note: Earlier formalisation by the same maintainer, registered in the Palomar registry as PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000026 (commit 3797cb6e4f8653744c0aa8e66ec8eb3645e75dcd): at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational. The theorem recorded here implies it. This repository started as a copy of that one and reuses, unchanged apart from the module-system header and comments on their role here: the six trusted definitions (identical, so both statements are about the same zeta2), the shared statements and proofs (Zeta2Lean/Statements.lean, Zeta2Lean/Proofs), the proof of the prime number theorem (Zeta2Lean/Cited), and six of its pair files, whose lemmas on prime sums, a q-integral residue calculus and certified enclosures of log are used here (Zeta2Lean/Pair). The construction and the linear form, growth, denominator and nonvanishing arguments are new here.

Earlier formalisation by the same maintainer, registered in the Palomar registry as PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000023 (commit 2ae1bccb82f1f72ed7a7aeab3196aa1cdbee165a): at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational. The theorem recorded here implies it. The shared infrastructure of the pair repository comes from it: the trusted definitions, the statements and proofs of the convergence of J s, the translation formula, Lai's criterion and the Δ-calculus (the five files of Zeta2Lean/Proofs are identical to its files apart from the module-system header), and the proof of the prime number theorem.

Open mathlib4 pull requests by Terence Tao: #43046 (compactly supported functions are dense in Schwartz space), #43233 (the Wiener–Ikehara Tauberian theorem) and #43238 (the weak prime number theorem), at head 78e1b2bbd0d256081c926fccada84fd084653286. The files of #43046 and #43233 are vendored, with porting notes, in Zeta2Lean/Cited/Vendor/PNT. Once they are in Mathlib, the vendored copies can be dropped.
Indirectly: the vendored Wiener–Ikehara code comes from the pull requests above, which adapt it from the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project. This repository does not depend on that project.
